block.rationale: Fresh verification block. Stader queue state at capture: nextRequestId=8219, nextRequestIdToFinalize=8215 (ids <= 8214 finalized, 8215-8218 still pending). The three holders below exercise both value branches (ethExpected for un-finalized, ethFinalized for finalized) and prove the finalized-preference (the FINALIZED holder's ethFinalized is 9 wei below its ethExpected), plus real on-chain multi-request summing (the MULTI holder's two requests). ethExpected is fixed at request time, so the PENDING value is stable; the FINALIZED request could be claimed by its owner at any time, which would zero its position (fine for a pinned fork block; re-verify before any live cross-check).

instance.note: Mainnet-only — Stader's UserWithdrawalManager exists only on Ethereum. Standalone (non-meta) adapter. Denominated in WETH (the position is ETH owed by the manager once ETHx is burned; NAV prices WETH via ETH/USD). positionId = "" (account-global); protocolId = keccak256('stader-withdrawal'); positionKind = Supplied.

holders.label: PENDING
notes: One PENDING (un-finalized, un-claimed) request id 8218 → valued via ethExpected (the redemption rate isn't fixed until the batch is finalized).
request 8218: ethXAmount = 164.4923 ETHx; ethExpected = 179.475428570970280827 ETH; ethFinalized = 0.

holders.label: FINALIZED
notes: One FINALIZED, un-claimed request id 8214 → valued via ethFinalized (the exact ETH owed once the batch is finalized).
Here ethFinalized = 10.804926562492357347 is 9 wei BELOW ethExpected = 10.804926562492357356 — the inequality proves the adapter prefers ethFinalized over the rate-converted request-time estimate.
request 8214: ethXAmount = 9.9029 ETHx; ethExpected = 10.804926562492357356 ETH; ethFinalized = 10.804926562492357347 ETH.

holders.label: MULTI
notes: Two open requests (8196 + 8197), both finalized → exercises real on-chain multi-request summing into one aggregated leg (previously only mock-tested).
Also the holder used to demo the per-request-id dashboard drill-down: the leg shows two sub-rows (#8196 + #8197) that sum back to the aggregate.
request 8196: ethFinalized = 109058136469367 wei; request 8197: ethFinalized = 218116272938735 wei.

ground_truth.method: live UserWithdrawalManager reads (NOT a Python re-derivation)
ground_truth.detail: All three holders are pinned against the real Stader UserWithdrawalManager at the fork block. PENDING: oracle == userWithdrawRequests(8218).ethExpected. FINALIZED: oracle == userWithdrawRequests(8214).ethFinalized, which is strictly less than that request's ethExpected (proving the branch precedence). MULTI: oracle == userWithdrawRequests(8196).ethFinalized + userWithdrawRequests(8197).ethFinalized (real on-chain multi-request summing into one aggregated leg). Plus protocolId == keccak256('stader-withdrawal'), positionId == "" (account-global), PositionKind.Supplied, balanceOracle == address(this), and the leg denominated in WETH. The claimed-skip (owner == 0) path is covered with mocks in the unit test (test/balances/BalanceAdapters/StaderWithdrawalQueueBalanceAdapter.t.sol).
